title: Rigveda 9.12: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.12: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.12 is a hymn of 9 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 672v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.12.1-9 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 7, varga 38); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 672v
translation.original_text:
1somā̍ asṛgra̱m inda̍vaḥ su̱tā ṛ̱tasya̱ sāda̍ne | indrā̍ya̱ madhu̍mattamāḥ ||
2a̱bhi viprā̍ anūṣata̱ gāvo̍ va̱tsaṁ na mā̱tara̍ḥ | indra̱ṁ soma̍sya pī̱taye̍ ||
3ma̱da̱cyut kṣe̍ti̱ sāda̍ne̱ sindho̍r ū̱rmā vi̍pa̱ścit | somo̍ gau̱rī adhi̍ śri̱taḥ ||
4di̱vo nābhā̍ vicakṣa̱ṇo 'vyo̱ vāre̍ mahīyate | somo̱ yaḥ su̱kratu̍ḥ ka̱viḥ ||
5yaḥ soma̍ḥ ka̱laśe̱ṣv ām̐ a̱ntaḥ pa̱vitra̱ āhi̍taḥ | tam indu̱ḥ pari̍ ṣasvaje ||
6pra vāca̱m indu̍r iṣyati samu̱drasyādhi̍ vi̱ṣṭapi̍ | jinva̱n kośa̍m madhu̱ścuta̍m ||
7nitya̍stotro̱ vana̱spati̍r dhī̱nām a̱ntaḥ sa̍ba̱rdugha̍ḥ | hi̱nvā̱no mānu̍ṣā yu̱gā ||
8a̱bhi pri̱yā di̱vas pa̱dā somo̍ hinvā̱no a̍rṣati | vipra̍sya̱ dhāra̍yā ka̱viḥ ||
9ā pa̍vamāna dhāraya ra̱yiṁ sa̱hasra̍varcasam | a̱sme i̍ndo svā̱bhuva̍m ||
translation.text:
1To Indra have the Soma drops, exceeding rich in sweets, been poured, Shed in the seat of sacrifice.
2As mother kine low to their calves, to Indra have the sages called, Called him to drink the Soma juice.
3In the stream's wave wise Soma dwells, distilling rapture, in his seat, Resting upon a wiId-cow's hide.
4Far-sighted Soma, Sage and Seer, is worshipped in the central point Of heaven, the straining-cloth of wool.
5In close embraces Indu holds Soma when poured within the jars. And on the. purifying sieve.
6Indu sends forth a voice on high to regions of the sea of air, Shaking the vase that drops with meath.
7The Tree whose praises never fail yields heavenly milk among our hymns, Urging men's generations on.
8The Wise One, with the Sage's stream, the Soma urged to speed, flows on To the dear places of the sky.
9O Pavamâna, bring us wealth bright with a thousand splendours. Yea. O Indu, give us ready help.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 672v (numbered 94v by the scribe) (OPenn image 673, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.11.8 ‹-sicyase manaḥ-cit manasaḥ patiḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 673r (numbered 95r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.13.1 ‹somaḥ punānaḥ arṣati sahasra-dhāraḥ›. Verses 9.12.1-9 end on this page.
